At first, like many, I thought this game was a Terraria-Inspired game with not much individual merit. I couldn't have been more wrong - This game is exceedingly unique, playing more akin to 2022's updated No Mans Sky than anything else. With three unique realms of gameplay options; Mech Missions, Settlement Building and Crafting/Exploration. On top of those it holds background story that you can delve into if you so choose, down to the race you choose affecting ambient dialogue, and a light-handed guidance through its missions , that while never forceful, is both well written and enjoyable. Would very much recommend this game for someone feeling very disenfranchised with the current state of survival / building / RPG games.

I happily recommend this game to anyone who enjoys the genre.

No meaningful updates have been released for about two or three months.
Developers ban people on their forums for expressing any kind of negative opinion about Starbound.
While the core mechanics of the game are in need of serious work, Chucklefish is interested only in creating more useless different hats and reworking old characters models.
The game is terrible and every single component of it requires a lot of tuning and balancing.
Release date is being pushed forward again and again. When Starbound was released on Steam they promised they would release the game in 2013. After a few months they said "well, maybe we will release it in 2014". Now they say that it's impossible to release it earlier than 2015.

The short version: it's like a Jaguar. Lovingly but not robustly made. Expect it to break if your run it too hard.
The long version: oodles of content, extremely mod friendly, a fun gameplay loop of mining, harvesting, fighting, running, climbing, and just plain adventuring. On the other hand, mods are almost necessary to get the full experience, leading to a competing interest between features and stability. The core game is also not really optimized, so even powerful rigs may experience framerate drops.
This crudely sums up the game, and I can't speak to anything regarding Chucklefish, you'll have to judge that for yourself.
I came back after almost 10 years to see if they had made this game playable. Unfortunately, it's still unfinished garbage, but now it's also overcomplicated with built-in mods. What a waste.

Edit. There is plenty to love and plenty to hate about this game. It is a fun game with pretty unique core mechanics, but it is absolutely a rage game. Getting far enough to not get obliterated by mobs of animals that spawn in clumps on the planet plus dropping all your resources on death in the caves with no coordinates is one of the worst things i've experienced in any game, especially when you forgot to put your bars and other materials back in your storage which is difficult as well due to having 90000000 variations on things. The story isn't compelling or captivating and progression is inconsistant as h3ll, but you could have a good time betwixt the pain. It's easy to feel like its game over after your first death and any after but it will get better and you will get stronger, if you can tough through the hardships.

tl:dr - If you like terraria, get starbound
Starbound is a sandbox adventure game in the same vein as terraria, however not just in space but also with a full story. The game has a more piano and soft soundtrack compared to terraria and has many different components when it comes to mining, interacting, the works. However this game is still largely a lot of fun to play and mess around with, especially with mods like the saturnians (moth mod) or Frackin' Universe. Even without the mods, the base game still has a lot to add to it which helps improve the game even more, if you like terraria get this game.

Played for 422 hours and had such high hopes for this game. Unfortunately, the designer decided to re-design it and lock progression behind story missions... I felt it was more fun as an open world experience. Afterwords, it became a "dead" game and all development was ended by Chucklefish. Maybe it's fun with mods but I haven't played it since.

Terraria has for a long time been one of my favourite games, and if you like Terraria but are looking for a bit... more... then Starbound will have you covered. Starbound is the Terraria of space, with more planets to explore than you can count, multiple races to choose from, and soooooooooooooo many options for game play.

Want to fly around in space?
Want to explore entirely new planets and dungeons?
Want to meet exotic races and potentially wipe out their culture? (or just chill with them)
Want to run around in a mech or blow shit up in space with a mech?
Want to live out your Han Solo fantasies (let's face it, we all have them)?
Want to build your own space station?
Want to terraform entire planets?
Want to look super cool while doing all of these things?

If you have said yes to any (or all) of these, Starbound is totally for you. I've left out a number of things as I don't want to spoil everything for anyone who hasn't experience the majesty of Starbound yet, but I will also mention that the soundtrack is AMAZING! I honestly can't recommend this game enough, anyone of my friends I've gotten into it absolutely love it, and I'm pretty confident that if you're reading this and on the fence about trying Starbound, that you will like it too.

TLDR: The game is fun at first, gets repetitive, and practically needs mods to be fun after a few hours.

Starbound is a game with so much potential, and its such a shame that people were overworked on it.
In the vanilla game, after playing a little it gets really boring and, at least in my opinion, building becomes the only fun part.
On that, this games potential for building structures in incredible. There are so many objects and blocks to build almost whatever you want, and the mods only enhance that.
With the actual gameplay, however, it gets boring fast. You go to a planet, get the resource, build better armor and weapons, go to the next planet until you realize you spend 2 hours getting the best stuff and trivializing most of the missions.

I love this game, and I've spent so much time in it, but if you're looking for gameplay, get mods for it.

A fantastic Terraria-esque game set in the procedural sci-fi universe of Starbound. Build intricate bases, fight challenging foes, and customize any aspect of the world to your liking. Mod support also allows for even more adventures in this early access gem of a game. Highly recommended.

Huge in Scope & Devilishly Charming // Recommended as a refreshing mix of open-world survival & RPG

+ If nothing else, this is an extremely charming title
+ Planets enjoy a varying level of difficulty
+ Exploration is a thrill to say the least
+ Base building mechanics are clear-cut & intuitive
+ Boasts about as impressive a presentation that seems possible with a 2D platform
+ Overall progression is handled with aplomb by the developers & feels both challenging & rewarding
+ Plot is perhaps a bit simplistic, but still a joy to move through & feels well-paced if you stay focused enough to pursue it
+ Healthy enemy & wildlife variance
+ Massive variety between weapons that are fit to satisfy virtually any play-style (it's worth noting that the animations can be a bit clunky at times, particularly with melee, but I found that this is quickly acclimated to & shouldn't be a deterrent for most players)
+ Puzzles & side missions galore
+ Beautiful & appropriate soundtrack; often quite relaxing & never jarring
+ Matter manipulator is a great way to collect resources & build
+ Steam Workshop support

- Colonist NPCs don't have much use & don't exactly have a robust selection of dialogue options, which serves to rob the experience of just a bit of the immersion
- Fairly lackluster enemy AI
- Many of the "boss battles" were a bit too easy

When writing this review I only have 17 hours playing in this game. That may not seem like a long enough time to most. This game is so very addicting if you like these style of games. Which I do. Playing with friends or even soloing in this game, it's never ending fun. You can get completely lost just digging down into the planet trying to find hidden villages to loot. There are cons, with any game you come across there's always something you don't like. For me, some of the quests seem a little hard if you jump right in as soon as you get the quest. Gotta prepare, maybe even over prepare for most of the quests. I still very much like this game, I recieved it as a gift, and I absolutely love it. At this time, I have yet to move on from the first planet so no comment on how the exploring is.

There really is a lot you can do in this game, and you're constantly learning new crafting items. The gear is pretty extensive and very fun to see what they name everything. I love the outfits you can find. It's a really fun, cute, game. Solo or with friends.
Terraria for those that have replayed it way too many times. A bit too chill and repetative for my tastes, but somehow managed to clock in 100 hours.

No Man's Sky x Terraria, except also an AU where the NMS devs never fixed the game and did shady stuff and the community had to fix everything with mods.

Still as fun and addicting as NMS though. Recommended, but buy it on sale.

And if you don't like it after 12 hours of play, even after installing mods to fix annoyances, try the Fracking Universe mod-set before giving up on it.

Basically space-Terraria. I haven't played without mods in years so keep that in mind with this review. Lots of stuff to do. Do quests, play the story-mode, be a landlord, Become a space adventurer with a crew, etc. Definitely an improved experience with mods.

Hmm, well i played 30 hours of this game during "Early Access" and it was great
Upon updating to the full version or complete version , had lost all my characters , so was rather disappointed.
But the new version is great , Introduces many more features and runs nice and smooth on my pc . Very happy about this game tbh. 5*

I loved this game since its release and have always enjoyed playing it and finding all the secrets and nooks and crannys, but this game suffers from a bad problem. Its replayability. The game has a interesting storyline, and tons of things to do. Like getting some little bears teddybear, or baking a cake.

These definetly make the game more fun, but after these quests are done and all the others the only other fun you can really get out of it is playing with friends. Another problem is how if you've already completed the game once then all the special quests are already done. This was a problem for me and my friends and it was sadly something we couldn't solve. After beating the game all thats really left to do is either play around with cheats, friends, or mods. These can give some entertainment but soon become boring along with the game.

These are all problems, but I hope you do buy this game. The experience you get is truly worth it.

This game is amazing. The races are interesting, the gameplay is fun, the universe is rich. Literally never-ending planets to explore.

Downsides, it's hard to play Survival Mode alone. Dying and losing all your stuff is infuriating. For me, though, survival mode is the only one that feels rewarding.

I highly recommend. I also love the pixel art.

There is also a lot of replay value. I've started over many times and it's always different. SO fun to play with friends. This game is highly underrated and I wish it had more of a fanbase and more updates to it.

As an avid purchaser of Early-Access titles, I will admit that the system failed here. Too much hype too soon, and not enough product when released on Steam.

Gaming is my main hobby, and so I try to play as many games as possible. I bought StarBound (several copies actually) and had to deal with character wipes for several months following. HERE IS THE THING: the situation may be different now, but there was a window of oppportunity where my attention (and money) was present - that time is gone now. Now I am off to other titles.

To quantify actual in-game stuff I didn't like: it was too similiar to Terraria (at least when I played it), the code was horribly optimized, and the art was 'meh'.

The Best Upgraded Sandbox.Reminds me of Terraria but in Space Version ,Even its more Enjoyable with friends in Cooperative.Soo Yeah Guys if you love the Sandbox games like Terraria.Even with friends then you should try this one

Do you like Stardew Valley? Have you ever wished it was in space? Do you like Terraria? Did you ever wish there was "more space"? This is that. A few years a go, Starbound was kind of an unfinished game, but now with Fracking Universe its basically a whole new thing! Explore, mine, craft, collect, quest, build, decorate, buy, sell, kill, and save...but in space and on other planets!
I tried this game, the UI and lack of shortkeys is so bad. it ruined any desire to go further into the game.

Players praise the mods and customization, while the story and characters draw the most complaints.
